subject: interpreting hyperparameters from a spatial gamma model

messages.author: e68f166a319176d9
messages.subject: interpreting hyperparameters from a spatial gamma model
parts:
Hi all,
I am running a spatial gamma model and I'm having some trouble interpreting the hyperparameters from the model. The model formula is:

fgamma9 <- formula(pos ~ -1 + Intercept + fGearEF + fHabitatSC + fHabitatTrib +
                     f(Site, model = 'iid') + f(w, model = spde2))

and the output is:

Fixed effects:
                    mean    sd  0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode kld
Intercept     3.773 1.292      0.979    3.832      6.162  3.910   0
fGearEF      -0.906 0.122     -1.146   -0.907     -0.666 -0.907   0
fHabitatSC    0.381 0.215     -0.035    0.380      0.807  0.376   0
fHabitatTrib  0.724 0.417     -0.104    0.726      1.536  0.731   0

Random effects:
  Name      Model
    Site IID model
   w RGeneric2

Model hyperparameters:
                                                 mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode
Precision parameter for the Gamma observations   1.86  0.031       1.80     1.86       1.92   1.86
Precision for Site                             487.49 11.031     466.12   487.36     509.71 487.11
Theta1 for w                                    -1.25  0.109      -1.49    -1.23      -1.08  -1.17
Theta2 for w                                     5.65  0.022       5.61     5.65       5.69   5.64

Deviance Information Criterion (DIC) ...............: 1747.71
Deviance Information Criterion (DIC, saturated) ....: 3086.76
Effective number of parameters .....................: 18.98

Watanabe-Akaike information criterion (WAIC) ...: 1750.69
Effective number of parameters .................: 18.76

Marginal log-Likelihood:  -916.40
 is computed
Posterior summaries for the linear predictor and the fitted values are computed
(Posterior marginals needs also 'control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE)')

I understand the precision for the gamma observations and the precision for site to be a measure of the variation attributable to the raw residuals and sites, respectively (thanks, Tim), but I'm not sure how to interpret theta1 and theta2. I've looked through various resources, but haven't found a concise explanation for these hyperparameters. Can anyone explain these to me or point me to a paper or book that defines them?
Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] interpreting hyperparameters from a spatial gamma model
parts:
The interpretation of theta1 and and theta2 depends on the spde parameterisation, which can be user defined. The default parameterisation is theta1=log(tau) and theta2=log(kappa) in the spde formulation.
However, I would recommend using the inla.spde2.pcmatern() model instead, since that uses a parameterisation that gives the correlation range and marginal standard deviation instead, which is more directly interpretable.

Finn
